history.period: Uncertain antiquity (unverified; the standing structure is modern)
history.summary: Chandaneswar Temple is a famous Shiva temple at Chandaneswar village in Bhograi block, Balasore district, Odisha, near the West Bengal border and about 8 km from Digha. The presiding deity is a swayambhu (self-originated) Shiva lingam; the temple is built in Kalinga architectural style with a black Nandi. It is best known for the huge 13-day Chaitra/Chadak Mela each March-April (Pana Sankranti, the Odia New Year), when 3-4 lakh devotees perform all-night arghyas. WARNING - do not conflate with the DIFFERENT 'Baba Chandaneswar Temple' at Kansa village, Nilagiri tehsil, Balasore (documented by IGNCA with 10th-11th century icons); this entry is the Bhograi/Digha-border temple (pin 756085). The CSV town 'Balasore' is the district/nearest city (~84-88 km away), not the temple's location - town corrected to Chandaneswar.

name: Chandaneswar Temple
town: Chandaneswar (Bhograi block; CSV town 'Balasore' is the district/nearest city ~85 km away)
town_description: Chandaneswar is a village in Bhograi block of Balasore district, Odisha, close to the West Bengal border and about 8 km from the beach town of Digha. It functions as a cross-border pilgrimage hub drawing devotees from both Odisha and West Bengal, set in the coastal plains near the Bay of Bengal. The surrounding Bhograi area is rural, with fishing and paddy cultivation as local mainstays.
